abbasid.scene: A wealthy Abbasid merchant's counting room in Baghdad at dusk, c. 850 CE. In the foreground, a large dark walnut desk with a warm polished sheen, worn edges and fine grain, reflecting candlelight. On the desk: an aged, torn-edged paper account sheet with ruled columns of handwritten Arabic-style entries and figures (abstract, illegible), a reed pen (qalam) beside it, a small dark-glass inkwell, polished brass balance scales standing on a carved wooden box, gold dinars and silver dirhams in small stacks and a scatter, a brass dish of coins, a rolled contract tied with rope, and a beeswax candle on a brass dish giving warm light. Behind the desk: warm limestone and fired-brick walls with carved stucco and a recessed niche of wooden shelves holding glazed ceramic jars, rolled scrolls and leather-bound codices; a pierced-brass lantern glowing on the wall; a carved wooden lattice screen; sacks and bales of trade goods. On the right, a great pointed arch opens onto a terrace and the city: the Tigris river with boats, a lantern-lit market with people, palms, and a skyline of domes and minarets under a violet-to-amber dusk sky. Warm candle and lantern light inside against the cool dusk outside; strong foreground-to-background depth; historically grounded, no fantasy architecture.

record.scene: Same hall, same desk, same framing as the previous image, slightly later in the evening. A scribe's hand in a simple linen sleeve holds a reed pen and is finishing a line of ink on the manuscript; the ink is still wet and glossy. Brass scales, dinars and dirhams, inkwell and candle exactly where they were. The market beyond the arch is quieter, lantern-lit.

centuries-ledger.scene: The same workplace as the attached c. 850 image, about five and a half centuries later (c. 1400): the same room and the same desk, aged, quieter and more enclosed — a merchant's counting room. Architecture: the great pointed arch on the right has been walled in with newer, slightly different stone, leaving a smaller deep-set arched window with a carved wooden lattice; warm late-afternoon light falls through it in soft dusty shafts; only a hint of weathered rooftops is visible beyond. No market, no river, no sunset glow. Left side (keep it darker and calm): the old niche now holds worn wooden shelves of leather-bound ledgers, record books and tied bundles of documents; an iron-bound wooden storage chest stands low against the left wall; the old lantern bracket remains, dim. The same dark walnut desk, now older: deeper patina, fine scratches, faded ink stains, worn edges. On the desk, in exactly the place where the loose account sheet lay: a large open bound merchant ledger with thick cream pages, ruled in faded red and brown ink into neat columns of dated transactions, amounts and totals in handwritten script (abstract, illegible); the lowest ruled line is half written in fresh, glossy ink. Beside it: an ink pot and a quill resting against it, plus the old reed pen; a few worn coins; two folded contracts tied with cord and sealed with dark red wax. Continuity: the same brass balance scales stand on the right exactly where they were, now secondary, their brass darkened with age; a single short beeswax candle on a brass dish at the far left edge of the desk, burned low. Lighting: warm late-afternoon window light plus candlelight, deeper shadows, a still and quiet interior atmosphere; restrained brown, walnut, parchment and aged-brass tones.

centuries-printed.scene: The same desk position, eighteenth century. Panelled plaster walls, a multi-pane window with dusk light, a brass oil lamp. On the desk: a single printed merchant's document with blocks of type (illegible), a quill and inkstand, sealing wax, a pocket watch. Warm, soft, candle-and-lamp light.

centuries-accountbook.scene: The same workplace as the attached c. 1400 image, about five centuries later (c. 1890): the same room reached through the same doorway of time, now a busy late-Victorian counting office in a merchant house. Keep the same desk position and seated camera; the desk is the same kind of dark walnut writing desk, now with a worn green leather writing inset and brass corner fittings. Architecture: the old stone walls are plastered and panelled in dark varnished wood; the small arched window on the right has become a tall sash window with slightly dirty panes and a half-drawn roller blind, grey late-afternoon light outside; a brass gas lamp with a frosted glass shade glows on the wall. Left side (keep it darker and calm): tall wooden filing shelves and pigeonholes packed with bound ledgers, labelled document boxes and bundles of receipts tied with red tape; a tall clerk's stool. On the desk, in exactly the place where the medieval ledger lay: a large open printed account book with pre-printed ruled columns and headings, filled in with neat handwritten figures (all writing abstract and illegible); the bottom ruled line is being filled in. Around it: a steel-nib dip pen resting on a glass and brass inkstand with two wells, a rocker blotter, a spike file of paid invoices and receipts, a small pile of printed invoices with a rubber stamp and ink pad, a few coins and banknotes, a brass letter scale. Continuity: the same brass balance scales from the earlier eras still stand on the right, now an old heirloom pushed to the back of the desk. Period accounting equipment: a heavy iron copying press on a side table in soft focus, a wooden cash box. Lighting: warm gaslight plus cool grey window light, some haze and dust, lived-in and slightly untidy, not polished; restrained brown, bottle green, ivory paper and brass tones.

paper.scene: The same workplace as the attached c. 1890 image, a few decades later (1930s): a company accounts office in an office building. Keep the same desk position and seated camera. Architecture: plaster walls above dark wood wainscoting; the sash window on the right is now a large steel-framed multi-pane window with afternoon light and a city street beyond; a wall clock; a door with a frosted glass panel through which a manager's silhouette is faintly visible; tall wooden and early steel filing cabinets on the left (kept dark and calm). On the same desk: in exactly the place where the account book lay, a large open ruled ledger with typed and handwritten entries (illegible); a green-shaded brass banker's lamp on the right glowing warmly; a stack of manila folders and carbon copies; invoices on a spike; a rubber stamp and ink pad; a fountain pen; a candlestick telephone at the back; a paper-roll adding machine at the side. Continuity: the old brass balance scales are gone; one brass object remains — the brass inkstand from 1890. Lighting: afternoon window light and the banker's lamp, soft haze; amber, beige and dark-wood tones, lived-in, not clean.

mechanical.scene: The same workplace as the attached 1930s image, about twenty years later (late 1950s): a corporate accounts office in a modern mid-century office building. Keep the same desk position and seated camera. Architecture: the old wood panelling is gone — painted plaster walls in muted sage-grey, an acoustic tile ceiling with fluorescent tube lights; the big window on the right now has horizontal venetian blinds half open, soft daylight in slats; a framed organisation chart and a wall clock on the back wall; through an internal glazed partition in the background, soft-focus rows of typists at desks. Left side (keep it darker and calm): grey steel filing cabinets and a shelf of binders. The desk: the same large desk, now with a steel-edged laminate top in warm grey over the old wooden frame. In exactly the place where the ledger lay: a dark green manual typewriter with a half-typed sheet in the platen (text illegible). Around it: a black bakelite rotary telephone on the right, an adding machine with a paper roll, a small stack of punch cards, carbon-copy forms, an in/out wire tray, a desk lamp. Continuity: one brass object remains from the older eras — the small brass rubber-stamp holder or the brass base of the old lamp, pushed to the back. Lighting: cool fluorescent office light mixed with warm daylight through the blinds; muted grey, green and brown tones, lived-in, slightly worn, not clean.

computer.scene: A 1970s computer room, same desk position. Behind the desk, a row of mainframe cabinets with reel-to-reel tape drives and small indicator lights; an operator in the background. On a dark laminate desk: a beige CRT terminal at the centre with glowing green text on a black screen, a mechanical keyboard, a stack of green-bar tractor-feed printout on the left, a reel of magnetic tape on the right. Dark industrial tones lit by the green CRT glow.

enterprise.scene: A 1990s corporate office, same desk position. Fabric cubicle partitions in grey-blue, a suspended ceiling with fluorescent panels, colleagues' heads visible over the partitions. On a grey laminate desk: a beige desktop PC with a CRT monitor at the centre showing a spreadsheet with a line chart, a beige tower on the right, a beige keyboard and ball mouse, a few 3.5-inch floppy disks, a coffee mug. Neutral corporate blue-grey light.

internet.scene: A 2000s office at night, same desk position. Floor-to-ceiling glass behind the desk with a city at night beyond, lights stretching to the horizon. On a light laminate desk: a silver flat LCD monitor at the centre showing a clean online store layout (no readable text), a slim keyboard, a silver flip phone on the right, a bank card on the left. Rich digital blue tones, the monitor the brightest light.

cloud.scene: A bright modern workspace at blue hour, same desk position. Glass walls and pale wood. On a pale wooden desk: an open aluminium laptop at the centre showing a dashboard with charts (no readable text), a smartphone on the right showing an app, a tablet on the left showing a bar chart, a white coffee cup. Cyan, blue and white tones, soft screen light.

automation.scene: A modern office late at night, same desk position. A dark desk crowded with devices: an open laptop at the centre, a second monitor, a phone with many notifications, sticky notes, cables; several glowing screens around the room showing different dashboards and apps. The feeling is busy and fragmented. Dark digital blue tones, screen-lit.

ai.scene: The same desk position in a near-dark, minimal, premium room. The desk is now a single slab of black glass with a thin line of electric-blue light running along its back edge and a soft blue reflection on its surface. Nothing on the desk. Deep navy and black, faint architectural lines in the darkness, a subtle haze. Very minimal, very quiet, high-end technology company.

autonomous.scene: The same black glass desk and room, a little more light. A person in a dark, well-cut jacket stands to the right of the desk, seen from behind or in profile, reviewing a thin transparent glass display that glows soft blue; calm, confident, in control. Deep navy, black, electric-blue accents, clean white highlights. Elegant and believable, not sci-fi; no robots, no holograms.
